rules.title: Rules

info.shield: Shield sends lookups to Quad9, which refuses known malware and phishing sites. It does not block ads, and it replaces the server's DNS while on.
info.autoConnect: Auto-connect: uses your selected WireGuard server. Disconnecting by hand pauses it until you join another network.
info.apps: Apps direct: apps that skip the VPN connect directly. Banks often block VPN addresses, so payments can fail through a VPN.
info.reconnect: Changing Shield or apps reconnects the VPN for a moment.
info.stay: Stay connected: some phones stop apps in the background to save battery. Always-on VPN and an unrestricted battery setting keep G VPN running.

speed.info:
Measured by M-Lab, an open research platform. A test uses about 50 to 100 MB.

Public results: M-Lab publishes every test, including the IP address it came from, as open research data.

Provider comparison: after a test without the VPN, G VPN sends only the three speeds. The comparison service reads your provider and city from the connection and stores no IP address. Turn it off with the switch at the bottom of this page.

Through the VPN: with the VPN on, it measures the speed through the tunnel and compares it with your last test without it.

Video preview: the same picture shown at the resolution this speed can stream, using the bitrates streaming services publish. No video is downloaded.

devices.info:
Knocks on every address in your Wi-Fi's range and asks devices to announce themselves. A device that refuses still counts: a refusal proves it is there.

Names: from what devices publish (Bonjour, UPnP, Windows names) and from your router.

Unknown devices: Android hides hardware addresses from apps, so a silent device with no announced name cannot be identified. Check your router's device list for those.

New: a device not seen in your last scan of this network.
devices.needWifi: Connect to a Wi-Fi network first.
devices.title: Devices

devices.notAnnounced: Not announced. Your router's device list can name it.

ping.info:
How long one round trip to a server takes, measured once a second over the last minute.

Jitter: how much each answer differs from the one before. High jitter is what breaks up calls.

Loss: answers that never came back.

How: Android apps cannot send classic pings, so each probe times a connection handshake, which is the same single round trip.
ping.title: Ping

status.info:
Connects to each service three times and shows the fastest answer.

Blocked here: a service that does not answer directly but works through the VPN is blocked by your network or country.

History: the last 24 hours of checks from this phone, kept only on this phone.
status.title: Service status
status.outage: Even through the VPN: likely an outage
status.blocked: May be blocked on this network

trace.info:
Each stop is one router your traffic passes through on the way to the site.

Silent hops: many routers never answer these probes. That is normal and not a fault.

With the VPN on: the path starts inside the tunnel, so your own network and provider are hidden.

How: it uses Android's own ping tool with a hop limit, since apps cannot send these packets directly.
trace.title: Traceroute
trace.slowest: Most of the delay, {ms} ms, is added at hop {hop}: usually a long cable between countries, or a busy link.
